label: The rule that blocks moving a hub machine block is copied in four hubs and one copy drifted: sk-doc/SKILL.md:65, system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:50 and cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:78 carry the sentence verbatim including the schema handoff-ambiguity reason, while sk-design/SKILL.md:74 paraphrases it as "nor into hub-router.json, which is a different schema".

The forbid is hub-level only: every copy names moving the machine block into the hub SKILL.md or into hub-router.json, and since a packet machine block already lives in the packet own SKILL.md, moving it within that file is outside the rule wording; the advisor report conflated the two cases.

workflowMode has different key semantics per hub: sk-code (SKILL.md:69), sk-doc (SKILL.md:68) and sk-design (SKILL.md:80) key it by packet, while system-deep-loop keys it by loop name (SKILL.md:59) even though its hub-router.json resources point at deep-research/SKILL.md, so the canonical (workflowMode, leafResourceId) pair needs a per-hub special case.

The no-match outcome has three names and no shared enum: system-deep-loop writes hub defer (SKILL.md:48, hub-router.json:11 outcomes.defer), sk-code returns load_level UNKNOWN_FALLBACK (SKILL.md:110), sk-doc writes UNKNOWN_FALLBACK (ROUTER.md:405) and sk-design writes UNKNOWN fallback (SKILL.md:71), so a consumer joining hub decisions cannot key on one value.

sk-design restates the mode list a fourth time inside the hub: SKILL.md:54-60 is a four-column mode table while the same list is the registry modes array, the hub-router routerSignals keys and tieBreak, and the ROUTER.md intent model; nothing parses the table, so it is the copy most likely to drift.

The stale-compiled-manifest claim does not reproduce: compiled-route-guard.cjs reports all seven hubs fresh today including system-deep-loop, and the guard iterates the full hub list, so any hub SKILL.md edit forces a re-mint while a packet SKILL.md edit does not enter the hash at all.

Correction to the iteration 2 cost claim: registry lines per mode are sk-code 32.5, system-deep-loop 34.7, sk-doc 40.3 and sk-design 51.5, so growth is linear in mode count but the per-mode constant varies by hub with alias and toolSurface size, which means a JSON generator must be parameterised per hub rather than templated globally.

Readability: system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:54-58 places a 96-word build invariant about allowed-tools equalling the union of mode toolSurface grants inside the routing section, and sk-design/SKILL.md:61 opens a paragraph with the fragment "Four modes." after the table already stated it.
